glossary:akhirah.title: Akhirah
keyPoints: Says belief in the next life, after death and the Day of Judgment, is part of Islamic faith

glossary:al-fatiha.title: Al-Fatihah
keyPoints: Says Al-Fatihah has seven verses and is recited in every rak'ah of every prayer (Bukhari 756); schools differ on whether a follower recites it behind the imam

glossary:alim.title: Alim (alimah)
keyPoints: Says in South Asian communities 'alim' also means a graduate of a multi-year alim course, with 'alimah' for a woman

glossary:allah.title: Allah
keyPoints: Says Arabic-speaking Christians and Jews use the same word, Allah, for God

glossary:aqeedah.title: Aqeedah
preCheckFlags: Lists the six articles of faith (one God, angels, books, prophets, Day of Judgment, divine decree) as in the Hadith of Jibril (Muslim 8) but has no sourceIds

glossary:aqiqah.title: Aqiqah
keyPoints: Cites Bukhari 5472 (which names a boy) and leaves the details for boys and girls to a teacher; the ruling itself (sunnah or otherwise) is not stated

glossary:ashura.title: Ashura
keyPoints: Says the Prophet said fasting Ashura expiates the previous year's sins; cites Muslim 1162b, whose source note mentions only Arafah. Confirm it carries the Ashura wording

glossary:asr.title: Asr
keyPoints: Says the Asr window runs from mid-afternoon until sunset; schools differ on the start (shadow equal to or twice an object's height), and delaying until the sun yellows is disliked

glossary:awrah.title: Awrah
keyPoints: Says what counts as awrah depends on the situation and the scholarly opinion followed; confirm this does not understate the agreed core (e.g. navel to knee for men)

glossary:ayah.title: Ayah
keyPoints: Say-it guide 'AH-yah' does not double the long a (AA-yah) as the page's pronunciation key does elsewhere

glossary:barakah.title: Barakah
keyPoints: Say-it guide 'ba-ra-kah' is the only one with no stressed syllable in capitals (BA-ra-kah)

glossary:barzakh.title: Barzakh
keyPoints: Defines barzakh as the in-between stage from death until the Day of Resurrection (Quran 23:100)

glossary:bidah.title: Bid'ah
keyPoints: Limits bid'ah to worship or belief with no sound basis in Quran or Sunnah; the Sunni difference over 'good innovation' (bid'ah hasanah) is not mentioned, and there are no sourceIds

glossary:bismillah.title: Bismillah
keyPoints: Says Muslims say bismillah before eating, before wudu and before any task; only eating is sourced (Bukhari 5376)
Says Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim opens Al-Fatihah; the schools differ on whether it is a verse of the Fatihah

glossary:burqa-niqab.title: Burqa / Niqab
keyPoints: Says opinions on niqab and burqa differ 'by culture and by scholar'
Arabic برقع is read burqu'; the say-it guide 'BUR-qah' follows the English and Urdu form. Confirm which to show

glossary:jam.title: Combining prayers (jam')
keyPoints: Says the Shafi'i school allows combining on a journey with conditions and the Hanafi only at Arafah and Muzdalifah; the Maliki and Hanbali positions are not given
Say-it guide 'JAM' drops the final ayn shown in the term (jam')

glossary:daif.title: Da'if
keyPoints: Says a weak hadith is not used on its own to establish a ruling (many scholars accept weak hadith for virtuous deeds, with conditions)

glossary:dajjal.title: Dajjal
keyPoints: Says Muslims are taught to seek Allah's protection from the Dajjal's trial (e.g. the dua before the final salam, Muslim 588); no sourceIds
preCheckFlags: seeAlso links to 'qiyam' (standing in prayer), which is unrelated; probably meant Qiyamah (Day of Resurrection), which has no glossary entry

glossary:dhikr.title: Dhikr
keyPoints: Says dhikr can be done anywhere and at any time (spoken dhikr in the toilet is disliked)

glossary:dhul-hijjah.title: Dhul-Hijjah
keyPoints: Says the Prophet encouraged fasting the Day of Arafah, the 9th (Muslim 1162b); the recommendation is for those not performing Hajj

glossary:dua.title: Dua
keyPoints: Says dua can be made at any time, in any language and in your own words; within salah the schools differ on non-Arabic or free-form dua
Say-it guide 'doo-AH' marks the u long and the final a short; du'aa has a short u, an ayn and a long final a

glossary:fard.title: Fard
keyPoints: Says doing a fard act is rewarded and deliberately abandoning it without excuse is sinful

glossary:fatwa.title: Fatwa
keyPoints: Calls a fatwa 'non-binding'; confirm the framing, since a layperson who asks a qualified mufti is generally expected to act on the answer
Say-it guide 'FAT-wah' ends in a short -ah; fatwa ends in a long a (FAT-waa, as in TAQ-waa)

glossary:fidyah.title: Fidyah
keyPoints: Says fidyah is feeding one needy person per Ramadan fast that can be neither kept nor made up, e.g. old age or lasting illness (Quran 2:184)

glossary:fitrah.title: Fitrah
keyPoints: Says every human is born in the fitrah, already inclined to recognise God, and that coming to faith is a return to it
preCheckFlags: Paraphrases the hadith 'every child is born on the fitrah' (Bukhari 1385) and Quran 30:30 but has no sourceIds; the Revert entry already cites both

glossary:duha.title: Forenoon prayer (duha)
keyPoints: Says duha is prayed 'after the sun has risen'; its time starts once the sun is well up (about 15-20 minutes after sunrise), since praying at sunrise is prohibited
Say-it guide 'DOO-ha' marks the u long and the final a short; duhaa has a short u and a long final a

glossary:ghusl.title: Ghusl
keyPoints: Says ghusl is required after 'marital intimacy', menstruation and post-natal bleeding; the Janabah entry says any intercourse or sexual discharge, so align the wording
Says ghusl after accepting Islam is recommended and 'some schools require it' (Hanbali; others require it if the person was in janabah)

glossary:hafiz.title: Hafiz
keyPoints: Says a hafiz is not necessarily a scholar who can give rulings

glossary:hajj.title: Hajj
keyPoints: Says Hajj 'should' be made once by every Muslim physically and financially able; it is obligatory (fard) once in a lifetime (Quran 3:97, not cited)

glossary:halaqa.title: Halaqa
keyPoints: Say-it guide 'HA-la-qah' follows the spoken form halaqa; standard Arabic حلقة is usually halqah (HAL-qah). Confirm which to show
Says many masjids run a halaqa for new Muslims

glossary:haram.title: Haram
keyPoints: Names alcohol and pork as examples of haram and says these boundaries protect your well-being

glossary:hawl.title: Hawl
keyPoints: Says zakat is due on wealth at or above the nisab once held for one full lunar year (cites Islamic Relief Canada)

glossary:hayd.title: Hayd
keyPoints: Says a menstruating woman does not pray or fast and does not make up missed prayers; it does not say that missed fasts are made up later

glossary:hijab.title: Hijab
keyPoints: Describes the headscarf as worn by 'many Muslim women as an expression of modesty and faith' without saying the four schools hold covering the hair obligatory; confirm framing

glossary:hijri.title: Hijri calendar
keyPoints: Says each month starts with the new moon; in practice it starts with the sighting or calculation of the new crescent, and Canadian masjids differ on method
Arabic gives the full phrase at-taqwim al-hijri while the say-it guide covers only 'hijri'

glossary:honorifics.title: Honorifics (SAW, PBUH, SWT, RA, AS)
keyPoints: Transliterates sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, subhanahu wa ta'ala, alayhis-salam and radiyallahu anhu, with meanings
Says alayhis-salam follows other prophets and angels, and radiyallahu anhu the Companions (cites Quran 33:56 and 9:100)

glossary:itikaf.title: I'tikaf
keyPoints: Cites Quran 2:187, whose source note covers only the dawn-to-sunset fast (the verse does mention i'tikaf); 'last ten nights' is from hadith, e.g. Bukhari 2026
Says many masjids let people join for a night or a few hours; the schools differ on a minimum duration

glossary:iddah.title: Iddah
keyPoints: Covers the waiting period after divorce and after a husband's death but cites only Quran 2:228 (divorce); the widow's iddah is in Quran 2:234

glossary:ihram.title: Ihram
keyPoints: Say-it guide 'ih-HRAAM' repeats the h; the syllables are ih-RAAM

glossary:ihsan.title: Ihsan
keyPoints: Say-it guide 'ih-HSAAN' repeats the h; the syllables are ih-SAAN
preCheckFlags: Paraphrases the Hadith of Jibril ('as if you see Him... He sees you', Muslim 8 / Bukhari 50) but has no sourceIds

glossary:iman.title: Iman
keyPoints: Says iman 'rises and falls in everyone': the majority Sunni view; the Hanafi-Maturidi creed (e.g. al-Tahawi) holds its core does not increase or decrease
preCheckFlags: Lists the six articles of faith in the wording of the Hadith of Jibril (Muslim 8) but has no sourceIds

glossary:isha.title: Isha
keyPoints: Says Isha can be prayed until midnight or, if needed, until just before Fajr; the schools differ on the preferred end (a third of the night or midnight)

glossary:islam.title: Islam
keyPoints: Says the word comes from a root meaning 'peace' and 'submission'; linguistically islam means submission, with salam (peace) from the same root

glossary:isra-and-miraj.title: Isra and Mi'raj
keyPoints: Cites only Quran 17:1, which covers the Isra; the ascent (Mi'raj) rests on hadith such as Bukhari 3207 and Muslim 162

glossary:istighfar.title: Istighfar
keyPoints: Says the Prophet asked forgiveness more than seventy times a day (Bukhari 6307)

glossary:istihadah.title: Istihadah
keyPoints: Says a woman with bleeding outside her normal period, such as spotting or very long bleeding, still prays and fasts (Bukhari 306)

glossary:istikhara.title: Istikhara
keyPoints: Says istikhara is for choosing between permissible options; no sourceIds (the prayer is taught in Bukhari 1162)

glossary:istinja.title: Istinja
keyPoints: Defines istinja as washing with water, with toilet paper 'first'; the four schools also accept wiping with paper or stones alone if the mess has not spread

glossary:jahannam.title: Jahannam
keyPoints: Says Jahannam is for those who reject truth and persist in grave wrongdoing; it does not distinguish lasting punishment for disbelief from temporary punishment of sinful believers

glossary:janabah.title: Janabah
keyPoints: Says janabah follows intercourse or 'a sexual discharge' and needs ghusl before praying (Quran 5:6); that pre-seminal fluid (madhy) needs only wudu is not stated

glossary:jihad.title: Jihad
keyPoints: Says jihad can mean inner struggle and, 'in some contexts', armed struggle under strict ethical rules; it does not say armed jihad is only for a legitimate authority, never individuals

glossary:jinn.title: Jinn
keyPoints: Says jinn are unseen beings created from smokeless fire who, like humans, have free will, some believing and some not
preCheckFlags: Paraphrases Quran 55:15 (jinn created from smokeless fire) and 72:11-14 (believing and unbelieving jinn) but has no sourceIds

glossary:jumuah.title: Jumu'ah
keyPoints: Says Jumu'ah is required of adult men, not of women, children, the sick or travellers, and replaces Dhuhr for anyone who attends; no sourceIds
Say-it guide 'JOO-moo-ah' writes oo (long, per the page's key) for two short u's and drops the ayn

glossary:kafan.title: Kafan
keyPoints: Says the Prophet was shrouded in three white cotton cloths (Bukhari 1264)

glossary:kaffarah.title: Kaffarah
keyPoints: Says the expiation for a deliberate oath is feeding or clothing ten poor people, or fasting three days if that is not possible (Quran 5:89)

glossary:kafir.title: Kafir
keyPoints: Says kafir literally means one who covers or rejects the truth and should not be used as casual abuse
Says kafir 'can refer to unbelief'; strictly kafir is the person and kufr the unbelief (there is no kufr entry)

glossary:khalwa.title: Khalwa
keyPoints: Says the Prophet said a man should not be alone with a woman unless a mahram is present (Bukhari 5233), so pre-marriage meetings include family or are in public

glossary:khimar.title: Khimar
keyPoints: Says Quran 24:31 uses the plural of khimar (khumur) when telling believing women to draw their coverings over their chests

glossary:khuff.title: Khuff
keyPoints: Says wiping over leather khuffs is valid if put on after wudu and the schools differ on other socks; the time limit is not given and the cited SeekersGuidance source is review-needed

glossary:khula.title: Khul'
keyPoints: Says khul' is divorce the wife asks for, usually by returning the mahr, based on the wife of Thabit ibn Qays (Bukhari 5273)
Advises speaking to a qualified imam and to a lawyer about Canadian law

glossary:khutbah.title: Khutbah
keyPoints: Says listening quietly is 'encouraged'; the Hanafi, Maliki and Hanbali schools hold silence during the Friday khutbah obligatory (e.g. Bukhari 934)
Says the khutbah is given 'during Eid prayers'; the Eid khutbah comes after the Eid prayer

glossary:laylat-al-qadr.title: Laylat al-Qadr
keyPoints: Says the Quran was first revealed on this night and, per Surah al-Qadr, it is better than a thousand months; 'the last ten nights' is from hadith not cited (e.g. Bukhari 2017)

glossary:madhab.title: Madhhab
keyPoints: States that the site presents differences between the four Sunni schools without choosing between them

glossary:mahr.title: Mahr
keyPoints: Says the mahr is the bride's right and belongs to her alone; no sourceIds (Quran 4:4)

glossary:mahram.title: Mahram
keyPoints: Says a non-Muslim father or brother is still mahram, and that cousins and brothers-in-law are not
Cites only Quran 4:23; relaxing covering before mahrams and the in-law list are in 24:31, and foster (milk) relatives are not mentioned

glossary:makruh.title: Makruh
keyPoints: Says doing a makruh act 'is not usually sinful'; the Hanafi school's makruh tahriman is close to haram and sinful, so confirm the hedge

glossary:maqasid.title: Maqasid
keyPoints: Lists the objectives as faith, life, intellect, family and property; 'family' stands for the classical lineage (nasl)

glossary:masbuq.title: Masbuq
keyPoints: Defines masbuq as anyone who joins after the prayer has started; strictly it is one who missed a rak'ah (catching the bowing counts as catching the rak'ah)
Says to stand after the imam's salam and complete what was missed (Bukhari 636)

glossary:mashbooh.title: Mashbooh
keyPoints: Paraphrases Bukhari 52 on doubtful things; the hadith's word is mushtabihat, while 'mashbooh' is the modern halal-certification term
Gives gelatin from an unnamed source as an example of doubtful food

glossary:masjid.title: Masjid
keyPoints: Tells readers they need no permission or invitation to walk into a masjid

glossary:mawlid.title: Mawlid
keyPoints: Says scholars differ on whether and how to celebrate the Mawlid and advises asking a trusted teacher rather than arguing online

glossary:mubah.title: Mubah
keyPoints: Say-it guide 'moo-BAAH' writes oo (long, per the page's key) for a short u (mu-BAAH)

glossary:muhammad.title: Muhammad
keyPoints: States he is the final Prophet and Messenger; no sourceIds (Quran 33:40, 'Seal of the Prophets')

glossary:muslim.title: Muslim
keyPoints: Says 'Muslim' means one who finds peace through surrender to God and that anyone who has said the Shahada is now Muslim

glossary:najasah.title: Najasah
keyPoints: Says impurities such as urine and stool must be washed off body, clothes and place of prayer before praying, and that this differs from lacking wudu

glossary:nifas.title: Nifas
keyPoints: Says the rules for bleeding after birth are close to those of menstruation; the maximum (40 days for Hanafi and Hanbali, 60 for Shafi'i and Maliki) is not given

glossary:nikah.title: Nikah
keyPoints: Says the nikah 'makes the marriage lawful'; Canadian civil validity depends on provincial rules (e.g. licence or banns and an authorised officiant), which are not mentioned

glossary:nisab.title: Nisab
keyPoints: Says nisab is measured against gold or silver; which one to use (silver gives a far lower threshold) is not stated (cites Islamic Relief Canada)

glossary:niyyah.title: Niyyah
keyPoints: Says niyyah is set in the heart and need not be spoken aloud; the schools differ on whether saying it quietly is recommended
Opening line echoes the hadith 'actions are by intentions' (Bukhari 1), which is not cited

glossary:qadr.title: Qadr
keyPoints: Defines belief in qadr as Allah's knowledge and determination of all things; no sourceIds (one of the six articles, Muslim 8)

glossary:qari.title: Qari
keyPoints: Says a beautiful voice and good tajweed do not make someone a scholar who can give rulings

glossary:quran.title: Quran
keyPoints: Says the Quran is 'believed to be' the literal word of God, revealed over 23 years; confirm the distancing wording and the figure (no sourceIds)
Says it is 'traditionally' recited in Arabic; recitation in salah must be in Arabic in all four schools

glossary:ramadan.title: Ramadan
keyPoints: Tells new Muslims they 'can build up to it at your own pace'; confirm this cannot be read as permission to skip obligatory fasts

glossary:rawatib.title: Regular sunnah prayers (rawatib)
keyPoints: Says the schools count the regular sunnah prayers a little differently (e.g. 10 or 12 rak'ahs a day)

glossary:revert.title: Revert and convert
keyPoints: Cites Bukhari 1385 and Quran 30:30 for every child being born on the fitrah, the basis of 'revert'
Says both 'revert' and 'convert' are fine and no one needs correcting (cites an Islam21c opinion piece)

glossary:riba.title: Riba
keyPoints: Says riba is forbidden 'in certain financial transactions' and describes it as 'exploitative or interest-bearing dealings'; confirm it is clear that any stipulated loan interest is riba
No sourceIds for a major prohibition (Quran 2:275-279)

glossary:riya.title: Riya
keyPoints: Says worrying that you might be showing off is not the same as doing it (reassurance relevant to waswas)
Cites Quran 107:6 and Muslim 2985 (hadith qudsi) for the warning against riya

glossary:ruku.title: Ruku'
keyPoints: Say-it guide 'roo-KOO' writes oo for the first u, which is short (ru-KOO'), and drops the final ayn

glossary:sai.title: Sa'i
keyPoints: Cites Quran 2:158, which names Safa and Marwah but not the seven circuits

glossary:sadaqah.title: Sadaqah
keyPoints: Says sadaqah is not obligatory, unlike zakat (zakat al-fitr, also called sadaqah in hadith, is obligatory)
preCheckFlags: Says sadaqah can be as simple as a smile and every act of goodness counts, echoing Tirmidhi 1956 and Bukhari 6021, but has no sourceIds

glossary:sahih.title: Sahih
keyPoints: Defines sahih as a sound, connected chain of reliable narrators; the standard definition also requires no hidden defect ('illah) or irregularity (shudhudh)

glossary:sajdah.title: Sajdah
keyPoints: Lists forehead, nose, hands, knees and toes on the ground, matching the seven body parts in Bukhari 812 (not cited)
preCheckFlags: Says prostration is one of the closest moments of a servant to Allah, paraphrasing Muslim 482, but has no sourceIds

glossary:salaf.title: Salaf
keyPoints: Defines the salaf as the Companions, their students and the next generation, the 'best generations' of Bukhari 2652 (not cited)

glossary:salah.title: Salah
keyPoints: Says 'it is okay to start slowly and build up'; confirm this reads as learning gradually, not as permission to leave any of the five obligatory prayers

glossary:salam.title: Salam
keyPoints: Transliterates As-salamu alaykum ('Peace be upon you') and the reply Wa alaykum as-salam

glossary:salawat.title: Salawat
keyPoints: Says the Quran tells believers to send blessings on the Prophet (33:56); also cites Tirmidhi 3546 (hasan sahih gharib per at-Tirmidhi)

glossary:sawm.title: Sawm
keyPoints: Says fasting is abstaining from food, drink and 'other physical needs' from dawn to sunset; the euphemism stands for sexual relations

glossary:shahada.title: Shahada
keyPoints: Gives the English wording 'no god but Allah, and Muhammad is His messenger' and says saying it sincerely is how a person enters Islam; no sourceIds

glossary:shaykh.title: Shaykh (shaykha)
keyPoints: Says titles are not regulated and it is fine to ask where someone studied (cites Qalam Institute and MuslimMatters)

glossary:shirk.title: Shirk
keyPoints: Defines shirk in worship, lordship or Allah's unique attributes and calls it the gravest sin if one dies unrepentant; no sourceIds (Quran 4:48)

glossary:qasr.title: Shortening the prayer (qasr)
keyPoints: Says Dhuhr, Asr and Isha are shortened to two rak'ahs while travelling; whether shortening is required (Hanafi) or optional (other schools) is not stated
preCheckFlags: Say-it guide 'KAS-r' writes k for the qaf in قصر; the page's key uses q for qaf (qur-AAN), and kasr is a different Arabic word. Expected QAS-r

glossary:shukr.title: Shukr
keyPoints: Say-it guide 'SHOOK-r' writes oo (long, per the page's key) for a short u

glossary:suhoor.title: Suhoor
keyPoints: Says suhoor is recommended; no sourceIds (e.g. Bukhari 1923: there is blessing in suhoor)

glossary:sunnah.title: Sunnah
keyPoints: Does not mention the fiqh sense of 'sunnah' (a recommended, non-obligatory act), which new Muslims hear constantly
Say-it guide 'SOON-nah' writes oo (long, per the page's key) for a short u

glossary:sutrah.title: Sutrah
keyPoints: Says to keep the sutrah close in front of you (Abu Dawud 695, graded sahih by al-Albani)

glossary:taziyah.title: Ta'ziyah
keyPoints: Quotes the Prophet to his daughter: what Allah takes is His, and what He gives is His (Bukhari 1284); in the hadith her child was dying

glossary:tahajjud.title: Tahajjud
keyPoints: Says tahajjud is usually after some sleep, is not required, and even two rak'ahs count (cites Quran 17:79)

glossary:talaq.title: Talaq
keyPoints: Says talaq rules have several stages and differ between schools, and advises a qualified imam plus a lawyer about Canadian law; no sourceIds (e.g. Quran 2:229-230)

glossary:talbiyah.title: Talbiyah
keyPoints: Transliterates and translates 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk' (here I am, O Allah, here I am), citing Bukhari 1549

glossary:tarawih.title: Tarawih
keyPoints: Says masjids differ in how many units they pray and that you can join for part and go home (cites Yaqeen, a review-needed source)

glossary:tashahhud.title: Tashahhud
keyPoints: Says the tashahhud includes 'prayers upon the Prophet'; the salawat (as-salat al-Ibrahimiyyah) follows it in the final sitting, and schools differ on the first sitting

glossary:tawaf.title: Tawaf
keyPoints: Cites Bukhari 1650 (a menstruating pilgrim does every rite except tawaf), which does not state the seven circuits

glossary:tawbah.title: Tawbah
keyPoints: Lists tawbah as recognising the mistake, regret and intending not to repeat it; omits stopping the sin and restoring others' rights for wrongs against people
Says Allah is always ready to forgive; no sourceIds (e.g. Quran 39:53)

glossary:tawhid.title: Tawhid
keyPoints: Defines tawhid as Allah's absolute oneness and worshipping Him alone; no sourceIds (e.g. Surah al-Ikhlas)

glossary:tayammum.title: Tayammum
keyPoints: Says tayammum with clean earth replaces wudu or ghusl when there is no water or water would harm (Quran 5:6); the schools differ on what counts as earth

glossary:tayyib.title: Tayyib
keyPoints: Says the Quran pairs lawful with good (2:168), so food should be both halal and tayyib

glossary:udhiyah.title: Udhiyah (qurbani)
keyPoints: Cites Quran 22:36, which is about the sacrificial camels of Hajj; the ruling on udhiyah (wajib for Hanafis, sunnah for others) is not stated

glossary:umrah.title: Umrah
keyPoints: Calls Umrah 'voluntary'; the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools hold it obligatory once in a lifetime, the Hanafi and Maliki a confirmed sunnah

glossary:wajib.title: Wajib
keyPoints: Says wajib is 'similar to an obligation' and some scholars distinguish it from fard; in Hanafi usage leaving a wajib is sinful, and the other schools treat wajib and fard alike

glossary:wali.title: Wali
keyPoints: Says the schools differ on whether a wali is required (the Hanafi school does not require one for an adult woman)
Says the wali is usually the bride's father or a close male relative; for a convert woman a non-Muslim father cannot act as wali, which is not mentioned

glossary:walimah.title: Walimah
keyPoints: Says the Prophet told a companion to give a walimah 'even if it was only one sheep' (Bukhari 5167, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf)

glossary:witr.title: Witr
keyPoints: Calls witr 'strongly encouraged' (the majority view); the Hanafi school holds witr is wajib, which is not mentioned

glossary:wudu.title: Wudu
keyPoints: Lists the wudu steps 'in that order'; order is obligatory for Shafi'i and Hanbali but sunnah for Hanafi and Maliki; no sourceIds (Quran 5:6)
Say-it guide 'woo-DOO' writes oo for the first u, which is short (wu-DOO')

glossary:zabiha.title: Zabiha (dhabihah)
keyPoints: Says zabiha is slaughtered with Allah's name said (a condition in most schools, sunnah for Shafi'i); notes scholars differ on meat of Christians and Jews (AMJA fatwa 80178)

glossary:zakat.title: Zakat
keyPoints: Says zakat is 2.5% of qualifying wealth above a threshold (true for cash, gold, silver and trade goods; crops and livestock differ); no sourceIds, unlike Nisab and Hawl

glossary:zina.title: Zina
keyPoints: Says the Quran says not even to go near zina (17:32)
